video.title: SpaceX's $2T Case, Nvidia's Shock Selloff, America Turns on AI, Trump Pulls AI Order, Bond Crisis?
video.display_title_html: SpaceX's $2T Case, Nvidia's Shock Selloff, America Turns on AI, Trump Pulls AI Order, Bond Crisis?

thesis: AI economics have flipped from speculative to undeniably profitable — Anthropic is EBIT-positive and SpaceX's S-1 reveals a $15B/yr compute-rental business — yet public sentiment, geopolitics, and a brewing bond crisis are turning into the real constraints on the boom.

chapters.title: Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic; hypergrowth and profitability
Why Americans have turned on AI, anti-human perception
Trump pulls AI EO, US-China AI relationship, dystopian AI layoffs
SpaceX S-1 tear down! Three businesses and the case for a $2T valuation
Nvidia smashes earnings but stock falls, why people are shorting chips
Market update: Flashing red signals, oil, inflation, yields up
China trip flops, or was progress made behind the scenes?

insights.headline: Anthropic hit EBIT-positive at ~$100B ARR pace
insights.body: Gavin Baker cites the WSJ reporting Anthropic was EBIT-positive in the most recent quarter, with OpenAI and Anthropic together at roughly $100B ARR on ~80% inference gross margins — reframing the 'circular funding / no ROI' AI narrative.

insights.headline: Recursive self-improvement plus continual learning are AI's two final frontiers
insights.body: Karpathy joins Anthropic to lead a pre-training team focused on recursive self-improvement — a model influencing its own training during a forward pass. Baker pairs this with continual learning (models learning from experience like humans) as the two unsolved breakthroughs that could 'pull the future forward.'

insights.headline: Stop asking model-makers; ask the factory worker and the nurse
insights.body: Chamath and a Shyam Sankar clip argue the AI PR problem stems from breathlessly interviewing AI inventors who all trade their own book. The fix is surfacing end-user wins — a third factory shift, an ICU nurse with more patient time.

insights.headline: AI backlash mirrors the post-nuclear distrust of science
insights.body: Friedberg argues AI is hated because it concentrates leverage in a few, with a diffusion lag so long the benefits feel asymmetric — echoing how nuclear weapons seeded mid-century skepticism of science, plus an 'anti-humanist' Copernican ego-shock.

insights.headline: A father used LLMs to find an existing drug that revived his daughter's neurons
insights.body: Baker recounts a hedge-fund manager whose daughter had a rare genetic mutation; he used LLM research to find a safe on-market drug that took her neuron firing from 30-40% to 80-90%, and is now using AI to design a complete cure he expects within months.

insights.headline: Anthropic pays SpaceX $1.25B/month to rent Colossus
insights.body: The SpaceX S-1 reveals 'Elon Web Services': Anthropic is paying ~$1.25B/month ($45B over three years, $15B/yr) to rent Colossus 1 and parts of Colossus 2 — effectively adding a second Starlink's worth of revenue. Either party can cancel on 90 days' notice.

insights.headline: The $2T SpaceX case is a flywheel of capital, tech, and execution moats
insights.body: Chamath underwrites the $1.75T valuation as a capital moat funding a technology moat funding an execution/learning moat: Starlink as core infrastructure, terrestrial data centers projected at $100-200B revenue by 2030-32, and Elon as the only 'civilizational-scale, one-more-thing' CEO.

insights.headline: Cursor's Composer 2.5 went Pareto-dominant after ~3 weeks of RL
insights.body: Trained on Colossus 2 with Cursor's proprietary coding data — allegedly more coding tokens than exist on the public internet — Composer 2.5 jumped outside the Pareto frontier in ~3 weeks on the same KMI base model, becoming Cursor's most-selected model.

insights.headline: A 'harness' is now as important as the model itself
insights.body: Baker defines a harness (Claude Code, Codex, the new Grok Build) as a runtime that manages state and memory — not just an app. In an agentic world it must be co-developed with the model, and lacking one left Grok behind despite a frontier base model.

insights.headline: Nvidia's 'share loss to ASICs' story is a benchmarking shadow
insights.body: Baker argues that stripping out China and comparing like-for-like, Nvidia's Western AI business is growing faster than Broadcom's (which guided 143% YoY). Rival ASICs aren't submitted to MLPerf or inference-max benchmarks because 'they will lose' — 'you can't fight shadows.'

insights.headline: The Nvidia quarter single-handedly saved the neoclouds
insights.body: Michael Burry's bear case said GPUs amortized over 4-6 years overstated profits. Baker counters that newer ASICs (Groq, Cerebras) handle decode in front of older GPUs, extending GPU useful life to 10-15 years and enabling cheap (~6%) asset-backed financing — a profound advantage.

insights.headline: A closing Strait of Hormuz is relatively good for America
insights.body: Baker's frame: as the world's largest oil/gas producer and exporter, self-sufficient in energy and food, the US is 'the best house in a bad neighborhood.' Every day the Strait stays closed re-industrializes America while crushing energy-importing Europe, Japan, and China.

insights.headline: Bond yields and inflation forecasts are flashing red globally
insights.body: The 10-year hit 4.6% (Bessent wanted sub-4%), Japan's 30-year at a record 5.1%, UK yields at GFC highs. Polymarket pegs 99% odds May CPI is ≥4.2%, with professional forecasters projecting CPI toward 6% — flipping the narrative from rate cuts to possible hikes.

insights.headline: Own ≤5 high-conviction companies; don't speculate on the rest
insights.body: Chamath's discipline: hold a handful (five or fewer) of concentrated long-term positions in businesses that represent the future, avoid speculation in any market, and ignore the daily 'vicissitudes' because the downside pain outweighs the upside sugar high.

quotes.text: Anthropic growing faster than any company in history at massive scale. And certainly any country. They're bigger than a hundred different countries for sure. And now profitable.
quotes.speaker: Gavin Baker

quotes.text: This was like from the PR school of retards. You could not have written a worse memo. You reduce humans to a label called the measurer, and then you're like, I'm going to lay off all the measurers.
quotes.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya

quotes.text: We're at the beginning of the beginning. He still has all these disparate assets... that thing will look very cheap, I think, in a few years.
quotes.speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya

quotes.text: The only people who are skeptical of orbital compute are those people who are not involved in data centers or space.
quotes.speaker: Gavin Baker

quotes.text: What is the point of being concerned when you have ridden the roller coaster to the top? The force of gravity is inevitable... we will throw our hands in the air and scream wee as we go for the ride.
quotes.speaker: David Friedberg

quotes.text: You can't fight shadows. Until we see a clean benchmark of GB300s versus TPU v7s, we're not going to know.
quotes.speaker: Gavin Baker

action_items: If you want to read the AI moment correctly, ignore model-maker hype cycles and track end-user outcomes instead — they each trade their own book.
When valuing AI infrastructure, check cross-sectional consistency: memory, Nvidia, power, cooling, and optical multiples can't all be right, so the gap tells you where the puck is going.
In a flashing-red market, concentrate in five or fewer companies you'd hold for a decade and avoid speculating on everything else.
Judge chip 'share loss' claims by whether the rival silicon is actually submitted to clean public benchmarks (MLPerf, inference-max) — absence is the signal.
